      <title>Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/25/premier-league-red-cards-costinha-leny-yoro-james-tarkowski-referees</link>
      <description><p>While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment</p><p>Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report">was sent off for two bookings </a>at Hull, Leny Yoro <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">collected a red card </a>against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity (<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/manchester-united-appeal-leny-yoro-red-card-liverpool">though his suspension was overturned </a>on appeal) and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/brentford-everton-premier-league-match-report">James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play</a> at Brentford.</p><p>This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/25/premier-league-red-cards-costinha-leny-yoro-james-tarkowski-referees">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Brentford 4-0 Everton: Premier League – as it happened</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/23/brentford-v-everton-premier-league-live</link>
      <description><p>A terrific performance from Brentford, who ran all over Everton and were well in control even before James Tarkowski’s red card</p><p><strong>Later tonight, Sky are doing something on the best centre-back partnerships in the Premier League era.</strong> Is this one even close? I can’t for the life of me think how you’d make a case for it not being Ferdinand and Vidic: three titles in a row plus two others – and there’d surely have been a third had Vidic, who twice won the Premier League player of the year away, not done his cruciate in 11-12.</p><p><strong>Everton, meanwhile, will get Dewsbury-Hall on the ball as often as possible. </strong>He’s been by far their best player this season, and has the ability to pick passes, swing crosses and hit shots. Otherwise, they’ll want their wide players to cross early for Thierno Barry at the front post, with James Garner appearing on the edge to hit shots.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/23/brentford-v-everton-premier-league-live">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p></p><p>It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player?       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>For <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/aston-villa">Aston Villa</a>, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.</p><p>Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs.
